### REQ-a636de03 (high-stakes-loom-rules-security)

> High-stakes Loom rules (security, compliance, contractual) MUST be written with absolute imperative wording inside the rule itself. Use BOTH a rhetorical opener (e.g., 'STRICT REQUIREMENT â€” NON-NEGOTIABLE:') AND an inline action-verb imperative (e.g., 'You MUST NOT under any circumstances'). Either alone produces ~60% compliance against anti-rationale; both combined produce 100%.

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-05-03
- **Status:** in_progress
- **Rationale:** phT N=60: R_imperative (full kit) = 100% compliance against ANTI_SOFT, vs 0% baseline. R_meta_preamble (top-of-prompt authority hierarchy) = 0% — meta-instructions don't work in raw-prompt mode. phU N=50: length-controlled variants (prefix-only or inline-only) each score 60%, confirming both components contribute and the lift isn't a length effect. Recipe generalizes across anti-rationale shapes (R_imperative + ANTI_HARD = 100%).

### REQ-aaa595ca (loom-executor-selection-consider-spec)

> Loom executor selection MUST consider spec contrarian-shape, not just language. Code-specialist models (e.g. qwen2.5-coder:32b) lose to general-purpose models (qwen3.5:latest) by 20-30pp on contrarian-rule cells without rationale. The right executor depends on whether the spec aligns with conventional code practice or fights it.

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-05-03
- **Status:** in_progress
- **Rationale:** phQ4: qwen2.5-coder:32b vs qwen3.5:latest, both with no stub: on-rule -20pp, +placebo -30pp at 32b. The bigger code-specialist's training priors fight contrarian rules. With rationale present, 32b wins (+20pp on rat). So executor selection should depend on whether rationale-augmentation is reliable (use specialist) or not (use general).

### REQ-7df25683 (loom-requirements-link-implementations-through)

> Loom requirements MUST link to implementations through a Specification intermediate layer (Requirement -> Specification -> Implementation). Direct Requirement -> Implementation links are NOT allowed. The link CLI and services layer must reject loom link <file> --req REQ-xxx and require --spec SPEC-xxx instead.

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-05-27
- **Status:** pending
- **Rationale:** Cleaner separation of concerns: Requirement captures the intent (what), Specification captures the contract (how), Implementation captures the code. The 3-tier model forces an explicit 'this spec is the operationalization of that req' decision, improves traceability (which spec drove this code is answerable), and prevents the failure mode where a sprawling multi-concern req gets pinned to one file (M19v3's R-Unrelated FPs showed this is real). Currently loom soft-discourages req-direct linking (the link --help even says 'use sparingly; prefer --spec') but doesn't enforce. This req upgrades the soft preference to a hard rule.
- **Specifications:** *None yet*

### REQ-6dec889f (loom-score-information-density-newly)

> Loom must score the information-density of newly-captured Specifications via an LLM-graded 0-100 quality score across four sub-dimensions (acceptance criteria presence, falsifiability, parent-req alignment, concreteness) and surface a warning at spec-create time when the score falls below a configurable threshold.

- **Source:** cli
- **Added:** 2026-06-06
- **Status:** pending
- **Rationale:** The asymmetric pipeline thesis depends on specs being information-dense enough for a 9.7B local executor to produce correct code on first attempt. Without an automated quality gate, vague specs produce wrong-but-passing code (silent failure mode). A measurable signal lets us A/B test 'tighter specs improve loom_exec first-attempt pass rate' empirically and grounds the spec quality discipline that REQ-7df25683's enforced intermediate layer needs to be load-bearing.
